name_reason: Compliant: data_fd2_ prefix + domain (tile_anim) + descriptor (table_base) for a base pointer into a loaded table resource. No Ghidra address residue (the only hex, 0x53A6D, is in the comment, not the name). The '3' is a resource index (domain meaning), not part of the symbol name. Name accurately reflects both purpose and datatype (a base pointer to a table).
purpose: Base pointer to the tile-animation palette-remap table resource (FDOTHER.DAT resource index 3), loaded once at startup and dereferenced during battle tile drawing to obtain per-frame palette-remap table addresses.
logic_summary: Zero-init (BSS) uint32 address slot. Written once in main() by fd2_load_dat_resource(fdother_dat, slot, 3). Readers compute a per-frame palette remap table as base + *(int*)(base + 6 + tile_anim_palette_phase_lookup[frame_counter]*4) and pass it to fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_remap_table. The resource blob is therefore a header of int32 offsets starting at byte +6, each pointing (relative to base) to a palette-remap table for one animation phase. Readers include fd2_composite_battle_tile_map (0x12170), fd2_blit_animated_tile_at_pos (0x12b8c) and several spell/animation routines.
datatype: uint32 (pointer-sized address slot holding a far-resolved buffer base; resource blob = int32 offset header at byte +6 pointing to per-frame palette-remap tables)
element_semantics: Single scalar: the runtime base address of the loaded FDOTHER resource index 3. Adding the int32 offset stored at (base+6+phase*4) yields a tile palette-remap table for that animation phase.
notes: src comment at src/life/main.c:1046-1050 is already accurate, concise, ASCII, and not contradicted by usage (base pointer of the tile animation table, FDOTHER.DAT resource index 3, uint32 BSS slot) -> kept. Ghidra data plate at 0x53A6D was null; created via run_script_inline PLATE_COMMENT (Java API + transaction) with a concise description consistent with the src conclusion (purpose + resource layout + dereference idiom + readers). No source edit was made (comment kept), so no clobber risk on main.c. Game writes the pointer (loader assignment) -> not const. Only writer is main(); 13 read xrefs in battle/animation render path.
